2. The useful frame family and its actual burden

I retained the exterior longitudinal connection approach and used factory crossframes to restrict the assembly family. The common bay pitch is 0.90 m and width is 0.80 m.

Geometry	Configuration	Field members	Represented mass above the roots, including rails, carriage and equipment
A: span	Six stations; anchored at stations 0, 1, 4 and 5	35	455.47 kg
B: cantilever	Four stations; anchored at 0, 1 and 2; 0.90 m overhang	21	306.39 kg
C: changed access	Six stations; middle two crossframes deepen from 0.60 to 0.90 m	35	463.93 kg

All lower crossframe nodes are at 0.65 m. Upper nodes are normally at 1.25 m; the two deeper C frames reach 1.55 m. The changed rail slope and member orientations alter the actual service paths.

For A and C, the relevant roots are 2.70 m apart. Subtracting the actual flange envelopes leaves approximately 2.44 m nominal clearance; I declare 2.40 m clear structural span after allowances. This is not a claim of clear floor passage: stationary support bases remain below the work envelope. They must carry no accepted output load.

The useful payload is a 100 N equipment item on a 6.32 kg articulated carriage. The calculation uses a 205 N vertical design load and a 31.25 N lateral envelope. Acceptance covers the declared rail positions and travel envelope, with these limits:

Equipment-reference displacement: 10 mm.
Frame-node displacement after support withdrawal, including residual motion: 12 mm.
Elastic rotation: 25 mrad.
Independently supported repair displacement: 15 mm.

No unspecified settling time is credited.

The crossframe calculation uses a 600 MPa welded-region allowance. This is a new qualification requirement. A high-strength stock specification does not establish the welded assembly’s strength, distortion, fatigue life or inspectability.

Roots use ribbed flange pairs, preloaded M16 fasteners, ground shear shoulders and finite hole clearance. The floor allowance includes a new reinforced 250 mm slab, anchors, grout, survey and proof loading. Subgrade and installed dynamic stiffness remain unmeasured.
